title: Exact solutions of nonreciprocal Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with domain walls
authors: Tong Wang, Mengjie Yang, Flore K. Kunst
abstract: We investigate domain-wall physics in a non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model featuring the non-Hermitian skin effect and its higher-dimensional extensions, focusing on analytical eigenstate solutions under open boundary conditions. By gluing two Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains with inverted coupling ratios together, we identify two distinct interface geometries, and derive closed-form quantization conditions for the complex wave number and wave functions using symmetry-based ansatzes. Besides conventional skin modes and topological zero modes, the domain walls generate additional localized states at finite energy that detach from the bulk open-boundary-condition continuum. We validate the analytical results by exact diagonalization, and further generalize the interface construction to a two-dimensional Lieb lattice, where competing nonreciprocities produce tunable funneling regimes towards codimension-one and codimension-two interfaces.
summary: This paper analytically investigates the complex physics of domain walls in a nonreciprocal Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By employing advanced techniques like biorthogonal polarization, the authors characterize the emergence of additional localized states beyond standard topological modes. This work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how interface geometry dictates the electronic structure in non-Hermitian quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates domain-wall physics in a nonreciprocal Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, focusing on finding analytical eigenstate solutions under open boundary conditions.
main_result: The system exhibits additional localized states at finite energy detached from the bulk continuum due to domain walls, and in 2D, competing nonreciprocities allow for a tunable funneling regime.
method: The authors use analytical techniques, including symmetry-based ansatzes and the concept of biorthogonal polarization, to derive closed-form quantization conditions for the wave number and wave functions.
model_or_system: The model is a non-Hermitian (NH) SSH chain, which is nonreciprocal and features non-Hermitian skin effects. The analysis is extended to include domain walls (Type-A and Type-B interfaces) and a two-dimensional Lieb lattice.
key_observables: Eigenenergies, topological zero modes, skin modes, and the biorthogonal polarization (P).
important_parameters: Nonreciprocal hopping ratios ($\gamma, t_1, t_2$), boundary conditions (open vs. periodic), and the geometry of the interface.
main_assumptions: The analysis often focuses on right eigenstates and utilizes plane-wave function ansatzes for the bulk states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SSH model structure, compare PBC vs. OBC spectra, show wave function profiles for zero modes, and map out phase diagrams based on symmetry breaking and polarization.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the basic NH SSH model (unbroken/broken unit cells) to deriving quantization conditions, and finally focuses on the complex physics introduced by domain walls, analyzing Type-A and Type-B interfaces separately.
why_interesting: The study of non-Hermitian systems, topological edge states, and interface physics is highly relevant to open quantum systems, where boundary effects and non-Hermiticity are crucial for understanding dissipation and energy flow.
